message.content: Logistic regression is a statistical technique used to model the relationship between one or more independent variables and a binary dependent variable (i.e., a variable that takes on two possible outcomes). It estimates the probability that a given input belongs to a particular class by fitting a logistic function (sigmoid) to the data. The model outputs values between 0 and 1, which can be interpreted as probabilities; a threshold (commonly 0.5) is then applied to classify observations into one of the two categories. Logistic regression is widely used in fields such as medicine, finance, marketing, and social sciences for tasks like disease diagnosis, credit scoring, churn prediction, and more.
